title: Exact scalar restriction on derived module sheaves is a right adjoint
statement: For a morphism φ:R→B of commutative ring sheaves on a small site, exact restriction of scalars D(B)→D(R), constructed by the exact-functor map on derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], is a right adjoint. In particular it preserves products. Its underived functor [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] is conservative and preserves limits and colimits of the site universe. The derived categories may use any common chosen localization universe.

source.place: Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint) for the identity of the underlying site; K-flat existence and tensor invariance in Tags 06YS and 06YT.

proof.text: The functor to abelian sheaves is conservative and preserves all limits and colimits. Under scalar restriction its underlying abelian sheaf is unchanged, so restriction is conservative, preserves limits and colimits, and is exact.

Use sheafified extension of scalars and its ordinary adjunction with restriction. K-flat resolutions give a resolving class on which extension preserves quasi-isomorphisms; the resolving-class essential-constancy theorem therefore supplies the left derived functor.

source.place: Tags 06YS, 06YT and 06YY: K-flat resolutions and everywhere-defined derived extension.

proof.text: For exact restriction, every denominator in the right-derived ind-diagram is inverted. The diagram is naturally isomorphic to a constant diagram (use inverses of the denominator maps); its indexing category is filtered by the calculus of fractions. Apply the general derived-adjunction theorem. Uniqueness of the right derived functor identifies its right adjoint with the exact derived restriction.

source.place: Tag 09T5, derived-adjoint-functors; exact restriction identifies its right derived functor.
